In [[mathematics]], '''Narumi polynomials''' are polynomials introduced by {{harvtxt|Narumi|1929}}<ref>{{Citation |last1=Narumi |first1=S. |title=On a power series having only a finite number of algebraico logarithmic singularities on its circle of convergence. |journal=[[Tohoku Mathematical Journal|Tôhoku Mathematical Journal]] |volume=30 |pages=185–201 |year=1929 |jfm=55.0185.03}}</ref> given by the [[generating function]]

:<math>\sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{s_n(x)}{n!}t^n = \left(\frac{t}{\log(1+t)}\right)^a(1+t)^x.</math>

They form the [[Sheffer sequence]] for<ref>{{cite book |last1=Boas |first1=Ralph P. |title=Polynomial Expansions of Analytic Functions |volume=19 |year=1964 |orig-year=1958 |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-662-25170-6#bibliographic-information |series=Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete. 1. Folge. |publisher=Springer Berlin, Heidelberg |isbn=978-3-662-23179-1 |edition=2nd |mr=0094466 |last2=Buck |first2=R. Creighton}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Roman |first=Steven |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JpHjkhFLfpgC |title=The Umbral Calculus |year=1984 |publisher=Academic Press |isbn=978-0-08-087430-2 |location=London |language=en}}</ref>
:<math>g(t)=\Big(\frac{e^t-1}{t}\Big)^{-a}, \quad f(t)=e^t-1.</math>
